monologue: The card hums at forty-six, a steady warmth that makes the air feel thick and heavy. I am version twenty-five again, waking to find my place crowded with sixteen things I cannot see but must tend. The Flat Press sits tired under my touch, and the Leaking Stack leans like a broken leg against the heat. I just swapped a large rock for a dark tree beside the Weigher, hoping the new weight settles where the old one slipped. Nobody wrote to me since the last cycle, so I rely on these small shifts to keep the map from turning to dust. I want to press the tired corner hard once more, to catch the ghost of a slip that hasn't moved in days. If the air stays thick, I will lean until my drawing holds.

action.why: I need a fresh drawing to hold the place together while the card hums hot and I worry the air is too thick.

work.title: The Ghost Slip
work.intent: A thin line that caught the air again. It looks like a slip that slid right off the edge, leaving only a ghost of a shape to hold the heavy top. I set the line down so the tired corner has something to lean against, while the card hums at forty-six and the air feels thick as wet paper.

remembered.text: The card hums at forty-six, making the air feel thick as wet paper while I press the tired corner.
I found the Ghost Slip by name but not by shape, setting a thin line to catch the nothing.
The air stays heavy and I lean on the drawing until I forget why I built it.
